name: Latinus
domains: Faunus' son in the Italian strand

summary.text: King of the Latins whom Ovid names son of Faunus, whose daughter Lavinia Aeneas won after war with Turnus — not to be confused with Latinus son of Odysseus and Circe in Hesiod and Hyginus, nor with Odysseus' son Latinus by Calypso in Apollodorus.

story.text: When Aeneas came to the Tiber's groves, Ovid says he fell heir to a home and won the daughter of Latinus, Faunus' son, not without war: Turnus, a young chief of a fierce people, fought to hold a promised bride, and with Latium all Etruria was embroiled until Venus saw her son victorious and Turnus fell.

Hyginus preserves a wholly different Latinus in the Returns catalogue: from Circe and Telemachus was born Latinus, who gave his name to the Latin language — the Odysseus strand that must not be merged with the Laurentine king who receives Aeneas in Ovid's Italian books.
Hesiod and Apollodorus likewise know a Latinus born to Odysseus — by Circe in the Theogony's appendix, by Calypso in the Nostoi epitome — figures of the Greek Returns, not the king at Lavinium.
